correctness.rationale: Read the full frozen RESULT.md and inspected verify.py. The two outward hemisphere normals at a site meet at Euclidean chord-triangle angle alpha_i; their intersection lune has area 2(pi-alpha_i), giving sum 4pi. The spherical Blaschke–Petkantschin shape-size disintegration (Akopyan–Edelsbrunner–Nikitenko, Lemma 5 and equation (9)) weights the uniform circle-angle simplex by chord triangle area 2r^2 product sin(alpha_i), so joint angle density is 8/(3pi) product sin alpha_i because its simplex integral is 3pi/8. Area-coordinate Jacobian is 1/4. For M<=m, each alpha_i >= pi-m/2; integrating the sine-sum identity over the truncated simplex gives the displayed CDF. Independently symbolically integrated normalization, mean and both boundary Taylor series, finding F(4pi/3+t)=9sqrt(3)t^2/(8pi)-9sqrt(3)t^4/(32pi)+O(t^5), 1-F(2pi-t)=t^2/2-t^4/24+O(t^5). The n=3 sampling has no degenerate atoms. A finite 350,000-trial verification is documented in the source VERIFICATION.md; I inspected rather than re-ran that Monte Carlo checker, and do not use its output as proof.
